newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee continues losing streak, ends down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee continues losing streak, ends down.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures, continuing a losing streak, posted sharper losses in late Thursday business on long liquidation after the market failed to bounce higher.
"Many were waiting for a bounce but it is not forthcoming at the moment," said a trader.
Some players had built up their positions this morning on hopes that the market would correct from an oversold condition and on better New York performance.
"But New York was weaker than anticipated," the trader said.
By the close, January was $11 off at $1,312 a tonne and just above a low of $1,310.
But most-active month March posted a bigger loss of $25 at $1,248, the session's low.
Jan/March spread widened a bit to $64 by the finish, up by $13.
Overall volume, dominated by the two positions, was 6,792 lots.
Pending significant news, traders said the immediate outlook for the London market, weighed by expectations of higher robusta supplies, remained weak and added any rise move was seen as a correction.
On the news front, some Swiss traders said Brazil's coffee harvest could exceed 30 million 60-kg bags in the 1997/98 crop, up from around 27 million in 1996/97 and 12.5 million in 1995/96.
But several others said while it was still too early to say, a figure above 30 million may be pure guesswork.

In other news, Brazilian coffee exporter Unicafe said the countrry's carryover stocks in private hands could be as low as 39,000 bags at the end of the 1996/97(July-June) crop year, down sharply from the 876,000 bags estimated carried over from 1995/96.
